steps.name: QC and exploratory checks on log2 expression matrix
caveats: Single batch, unpaired 6v6 design is small; do not over-interpret PCA separation as proof of a treatment effect
12000 genes is the full feature set delivered — do not assume additional unannotated genes exist
steps.context: Input is log_expr.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, log2(TPM+1), core-facility normalized) and metadata.csv (12 samples x condition: treated/control, unpaired, single batch). No raw counts exist.
steps.question: Do the 12 muscle samples (6 treated, 6 control) show consistent distributions, no obvious outliers, and expected clustering by condition prior to differential expression testing on the log2(TPM+1) matrix?
constraints: Treat the matrix strictly as already-normalized log2 data — do not re-log-transform or apply count-based normalization
Join metadata.csv to expression columns by sample ID before any grouping
acceptance_criteria: Per-sample boxplots/density plots of the 12000x12 log2 matrix are generated and show comparable distributions across samples
PCA or hierarchical clustering of the 12 samples is produced and sample-condition assignment (6 treated vs 6 control) from metadata.csv is checked against clustering
Any outlier sample is flagged with justification, not silently removed
Low-variance / near-constant genes are noted (not required to be filtered) so the DE step can decide on filtering

steps.name: Differential expression: treated vs control via limma moderated t-test
caveats: n=6 per group is modest power; moderated t-test partially mitigates but does not eliminate small-sample variance instability
No surrogate variables/covariates were provided in metadata beyond condition — cannot adjust for unknown confounders
steps.context: log2(TPM+1) values, not counts, were delivered — count-based DE tools (DESeq2, edgeR, PyDESeq2) are inappropriate here since they model raw count variance structure. limma's moderated t-test (empirical Bayes shrinkage of gene-wise variances) is the standard method for pre-normalized continuous expression data such as this. Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch — a simple two-group model with no batch term needed.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are significantly differentially expressed between the 6 treated and 6 control muscle samples, using the log2(TPM+1) values as delivered?
constraints: Use limma directly on log2 values (do not route through voom, which is for count data)
Model as a single two-group comparison (treated vs control); no batch or pairing term given single-batch unpaired design
Report both nominal and FDR-adjusted p-values; do not present nominal p-values alone as significance
acceptance_criteria: limma is applied directly to the log2 expression matrix with a treated-vs-control design matrix (unpaired, single batch, no covariates to adjust for beyond condition)
Output table has one row per gene with log2 fold change, moderated t-statistic, raw p-value, and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value (FDR)
Result is saved as a full ranked gene list (not pre-filtered to 'significant only'), so downstream enrichment can use it as a ranked list
Number of genes at FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| thresholds commonly used (e.g. 0.5, 1) is reported explicitly, without asserting biological significance beyond the statistics

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes using WikiPathways human gene sets
caveats: 12000-gene background may not match the WikiPathways gene universe exactly; report background size used for the test
Small sample size (n=6/6) upstream means pathway enrichment reflects an underpowered DE signal; treat results as hypothesis-generating
steps.context: Human muscle tissue dataset. WikiPathways human pathway gene sets (HGNC gene symbols, 2026.07.10 snapshot) are available in the reference store as a GMT file and should be used for pathway enrichment of the treated-vs-control DE result from T1S2.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes differing between treated and control muscle samples, using the ranked limma DE result and WikiPathways human pathway gene sets?
constraints: Use only the human WikiPathways GMT (organism must match Homo sapiens) — do not substitute mouse or rat pathway sets
Parse the GMT's '%'-delimited descriptor field to recover readable pathway names for reporting
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (e.g. fgsea-style ranked GSEA on the full ranked gene list by t-statistic or log2FC, plus a hypergeometric/ORA test on FDR<0.05 genes) is run against WikiPathways human gene sets
Output lists enriched pathways with normalized enrichment score or odds ratio, p-value, and FDR-adjusted q-value
If the WikiPathways human GMT reference is unavailable at run time, the step reports this explicitly and skips enrichment rather than fabricating pathway results
Gene symbols in the DE table are matched to the GMT's HGNC symbols; unmatched genes are counted and reported, not silently dropped

plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE from log2 expression
plan.analytical_narrative: The core facility delivered log2(TPM+1) normalized expression (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch) — not raw counts. This rules out count-based tools (DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial models, PyDESeq2) which require integer counts and would give invalid p-values on already-normalized log data. The correct approach for continuous, approximately-normal log-ratio data is limma on the log2 matrix directly (moderated t-test via empirical Bayes shrinkage), which is designed exactly for this input type. Track 1 performs QC and the limma-based differential expression. Track 2 takes the resulting DE gene list into pathway enrichment using WikiPathways human gene sets, since the research question is about which genes differ and their functional context.
